wx.name: Weather files
wx.notice: A typical weather year for a station near your model. It is what the weather is usually like, not a forecast and not the worst case. A compliance calculation may require its own weather file: use the one your authority names.
wx.place.model: From the model's site: latitude {lat}, longitude {lon}.
wx.place.none: The model does not say where it stands. Type the latitude and longitude (north and east are positive, so California's longitude is negative).
wx.sets.failed: These weather sets could not be read just now: {sets}.
wx.none: No station within 400 km in the weather sets this add-on has. Open a weather file of your own instead.
wx.far: This station is {km} km away. The weather where you build may differ: check the figures against local knowledge.
wx.high: This station is {m} m higher or lower than the model's site. Temperature falls roughly 6.5 °C for every 1,000 m climbed, so its figures will not match the site.
wx.fact.mean: Mean air temperature of the year
wx.ground.file: from the file's deepest ground temperatures
wx.ground.air: the year's mean air temperature, a first estimate
wx.src.station: The design temperatures are the station's published design conditions carried in the weather file. The degree-days are counted from the hours of the typical year.
wx.src.year: This file carries no published design conditions, so the design temperatures are the ones this single typical year stays above (or below) for that share of its hours. They can differ by a degree or two from published long-term figures. The degree-days are counted from the same hours.
wx.src.short.year: worked out of the typical year
wx.btn.own: Open a weather file of your own (.epw)
wx.own.note: Your own file, {name}. It stays in this browser tab.
wx.err.big: That file is too large to be a weather year.
wx.err.notepw: That is not an EnergyPlus weather file (.epw).
wx.err.place: The weather file does not say where its station is.
wx.err.hours: The weather file does not hold a whole year of hours.
wx.err.row: A line of the weather file could not be read.
wx.err.missing: The weather file has hours with no air temperature.
wx.err.fetch: The weather file could not be fetched. Check your connection and try again.
wx.err.sha: The weather file that arrived is not the one the index lists, so it was not used.
wx.err.gunzip: This browser cannot unpack the weather file.
wx.warn.design: The file's design conditions could not be read.
wx.bim.loads: Use in Heating and cooling loads
wx.bim.year: Use the year in the EnergyPlus check
wx.bim.none: None of the station's figures fit the boxes of Heating and cooling loads.
wx.bim.loads.done: Heating and cooling loads now uses {te} °C outside in winter, {ts} °C in summer and {dd} degree-days. Open the Daylight tab and press Work out the loads.
wx.bim.year.done: The EnergyPlus check now has {name} for a year's run.
wx.v.title: The weather year
wx.v.f.timeOn: Cut at a time of day
wx.v.f.auto: Fit the scale to the data
wx.v.f.period: Period for the wind rose, psychrometric chart and sun path
wx.v.set.bad: That is not a settings file of this viewer. Nothing was changed.
wx.v.set.nocopy: The browser did not allow copying. Use Show the settings as text.
wx.v.set.stored: The viewer will open like this from now on.
wx.v.set.cleared: The viewer will open with its own settings again.
wx.v.prof.year: {metric} through the year at {time}, over each day's lowest to highest
wx.v.prof.day: {metric} on {date}, over the lowest to highest of each hour in {month}
wx.v.rose.title: Where the wind comes from: {period}
wx.v.hist.title: Hours of the year at each value: {metric} ({unit})
wx.v.st.title: {n} stations, coloured by summer design temperature
wx.v.st.hint: Click a station to open its year. Shift+click to compare it with the one that is open.
wx.v.none: The file has no hours of this.
wx.v.nogl: This browser gave no 3D drawing, so the surface is shown as a flat map.
wx.v.keys: Keys: M next quantity (Shift+M previous). X, C, V switch the date, time and value cuts. B cut block. T, Y, U step the time, date and value (Shift steps back). 1 to 5 choose the view. Arrows turn, W and S move nearer and farther, A and D slide, F fits. Space starts and stops the animation. Click the chart to put the cuts there, or drag a cut by its line on the surface. Alt+click or Alt+drag sets the value cut. Esc closes. Times are the station's standard time.
wx.m.ir: Horizontal infrared radiation from the sky
wx.mh.wb: Worked out from each hour's dry-bulb temperature, relative humidity and pressure with the psychrometric equations of the ASHRAE Handbook. It is not a column of the file.
wx.mh.w: Grams of water vapour per kilogram of dry air, worked out from each hour's temperature, relative humidity and pressure. It is not a column of the file.
wx.mh.h: Heat held by the moist air per kilogram of dry air, counted from 0 °C, worked out from each hour's temperature, relative humidity and pressure. Shown in kJ/kg in both unit systems. It is not a column of the file.
wx.mh.dep: The dry-bulb temperature less the dew point: how far the air is from saturation.
wx.mh.alt: Degrees above the horizon at the middle of each hour, worked out from the station's latitude, longitude and time zone. Below zero is night. It is not a column of the file.
wx.share.unknown: The link names a weather station this add-on does not have.
wx.v.comfort.note: The comfort range is a plain range of air temperature and relative humidity that you set. It is not a comfort standard: it leaves out radiant temperature, air speed, clothing and activity.
wx.v.comfort.count: {n} of {of} hours ({pct} %) between {t0} and {t1}, and between {rh0} % and {rh1} % relative humidity
wx.v.cmp.none: Choose a second station under Compare with, or Shift+click one on the Stations map.
wx.v.cmp.nolist: No station list is loaded, so there is nothing to compare with.
wx.v.cmp.diff: The first station less the second (mean {mean}). Red: the first is higher. Blue: the second is higher.
wx.v.edit.note: Multiply or shift the chosen quantity for every hour of the year, to try a warmer year or a dimmer sky. Only that column changes: humidity does not follow a temperature change, and the design conditions in the file's header stay as they were. Missing hours stay missing.
wx.v.edit.nothing: Nothing is changed, so there is nothing to save.
wx.v.edit.nofile: The file itself is not at hand, so a changed copy cannot be saved.
wx.v.edit.saved: The changed file is saved. Its second comment line says what was changed.
wx.v.b.share: Copy a link to this view
wx.v.share.none: A link needs a station from a weather set. Your own file stays on your computer, so it cannot be linked.
wx.v.share.copied: Link copied. It opens for anyone who has switched this add-on on.
wx.v.share.shown: The browser did not allow copying. The link is in the box below.
wx.v.psy.title: Psychrometric chart: {period}, coloured by {by}
wx.v.sun.title: Sun path at {lat}°, {lon}°: each daylight hour coloured by {metric} ({period})
wx.v.sun.now: {date}, {time}: the sun is {alt}° above the horizon, bearing {az}°
wx.v.foot.cmp: Mean {a} here, {b} at the second station
